name: P2 · Previous-year papers — Computer Science (KEA / KSET)
description: Real questions from past KEA / KSET papers (178 so far): KSET 2023 – Computer Science & Application; KSET 2024 – Computer Science & Application. Typed from KEA's scanned question papers with the options in the printed order; each question shows its paper and number. Where KEA publishes no full key, the answer was worked out by ExamSim and says so. Each paper also comes as a full-paper mock test.

questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: 5 > 8 is false, so the second conditional is evaluated. < binds tighter than !=, so 2 < 5 = 1 and 1 != 1 = 0 (false) → x = 30. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: C does no bounds checking: ary[-1] and ary[4] read memory outside the array (undefined behaviour), so unpredictable 'garbage' values are printed. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: The template is instantiated for int (max(55, 60) = 60) and for long (max(105, 53) = 105). (With some compilers the call can clash with std::max; the intended answer is 60 and 105.) (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which of the following can be considered as the correct syntax for declaring an array of pointers of integers that has a size of 20 in C++?
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: new int*[20] allocates 20 int pointers and returns int**. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which of the following tag is used for inserting the largest heading in HTML?
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: <h1> is the largest heading level; <h6> is the smallest. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which is not a method in the life-cycle of Java servlet?
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: A servlet's life cycle is init() → service() (for each request) → destroy(). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: In true color RGB, the number of bits for color depth is
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: True colour uses 8 bits for each of R, G and B = 24 bits (about 16.7 million colours). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: ____ translates the DML statements embedded in an application program to normal procedure calls in the host language.
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: The DML pre-compiler converts embedded DML into host-language procedure calls (Silberschatz / Navathe). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Identify the correctness of the following statements:
I. The aggregate functions like sum, count, etc., can be performed with the basic relational algebraic operations of relational calculus formulas.
II. Relational calculus is a formal query language where the queries are expressed as variables and formulas on these variables.
III. The queries in the relational algebra are procedural.

options.A: I is correct; II and III are incorrect
options.B: I is incorrect; II and III are correct
options.C: I and II are correct; III is incorrect
options.D: I and II are incorrect; III is correct

questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: Aggregates are an extension beyond basic relational algebra/calculus; calculus is declarative with variables and formulas; algebra is procedural. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is false?

options.B: Triggers does not provide transparent event logging

questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: Triggers are used to enforce complex security, prevent invalid transactions and log events transparently. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which one of the following is not a desirable property of transaction?
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: The ACID properties are Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation and Durability; normalization is a schema-design process. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Identify the correctness of the statements:
I. Object-Relational Databases are schema-less
II. Object-Relational Databases store objects as rows in tables
III. Object-Relational Databases make use of pessimistic and optimistic locking

options.A: I is correct; II and III are incorrect
options.B: I is incorrect; II and III are correct
options.C: I and II are correct; III is incorrect
options.D: I and II are incorrect; III is correct

questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: ORDBs keep a relational schema (not schema-less), store objects as rows, and use the usual concurrency-control methods. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: A clustering index is defined on the fields which are of the type:
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: A clustering index is on a non-key field by which the file is physically ordered; a primary index is on an ordering key field. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The system of data warehousing is mostly used for:
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: A data warehouse is designed for querying, reporting and analysis (OLAP) rather than transaction processing. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The process of data scrubbing deals with the process to:

options.A: Upgrade the quality of data after it is moved into a data warehouse.
options.B: Reject data from the data warehouse and to create the necessary indexes.
options.C: Load data into data warehouse and to create necessary indexes.
options.D: Clean and upgrade the quality of data, before it is moved into a data warehouse.

questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: Scrubbing (cleansing) fixes errors and inconsistencies before loading into the warehouse. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are true?
I. Facebook has the world's largest Hadoop cluster
II. Hadoop 2.0 allows live stream processing of real-time data.
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: Both are standard textbook statements: Facebook ran the largest Hadoop cluster, and Hadoop 2.0 (YARN) supports stream-processing engines alongside MapReduce. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which of the following is a NoSQL type?
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: NoSQL types: document, key-value, column-family and graph databases. JSON is a data format. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: ____ translates the high-level language program into machine language.
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: A compiler translates high-level source code; an assembler translates assembly language. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: ____ is invoked when there is a need to perform process scheduling, that is when a process from the ready queue is to be selected for dispatching to the CPU.
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: The short-term (CPU) scheduler picks the next ready process for the CPU. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: A thread is a
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: A thread shares its process's code, data and files but has its own registers and stack – a lightweight process. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which one of the following is not a deadlock recovery method?
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: Hold and wait is one of the four necessary conditions for deadlock, not a recovery method. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: ____ helps to control memory wastage occurring in dynamic partitioning.
questions.subject: Q1–25
questions.explanation: Compaction shuffles memory contents to merge scattered free holes (external fragmentation) into one block. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: RAID level 4 provides:
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: RAID 1 = mirroring, RAID 2 = memory-style ECC, RAID 3 = bit-interleaved parity, RAID 4 = block-interleaved parity. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: ____ is a general model of protection that provides a mechanism for protection without imposing a particular protection policy on the system or its users.
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Silberschatz: the access matrix separates mechanism from policy. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: ____ is built into the software by the original programmer in order to gain access to any system without going through the usual security access procedure.
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: A trap door (back door) is a hidden entry point left by the programmer. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: A ____ acts as a lightweight operating system that runs natively on the hardware and manages guest operating systems.
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Type 1 hypervisors are special-purpose OSs running on bare hardware; type 0 is firmware-based and type 2 runs on a host OS. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: In a communication network, if a path from Site A to Site B is fixed for the duration of one session, the routing scheme adopted is called ____.
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Virtual routing fixes the path for one session; fixed routing always uses the same path; dynamic routing chooses per message. (Official answer: KEA revised key, 28 Mar 2024.)

questions.question: In the software generic process model, ____ executes the activities in a circular manner.
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Pressman: an evolutionary process flow executes the activities in a circular manner; an iterative flow repeats activities before moving on. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: ____ defines a problem associated with a framework activity for the process.
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Pressman: a stage pattern relates to a framework activity; a task pattern to a software engineering action; a phase pattern to the sequence of activities. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: ____ depicts the information domain for the problem.
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Pressman: data models depict the information domain for the problem. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: ____ architectural design model addresses the behavioural aspects of the program architecture, indicating how the structure or system configuration may change as a function of external events.
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Pressman lists structural, framework, dynamic, process and functional architectural models; dynamic models address behaviour. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: ____ is an indication of the relative functional strength of a module.
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Cohesion measures a module's functional strength; coupling measures interdependence between modules. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The extent to which a program can be expected to perform its intended function with the required precision. This definition belongs to ____ software quality factor.
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: McCall: reliability is performing the intended function with required precision; correctness is satisfying the specification. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The ____ is a dynamic multivariable model that assumes a specific distribution of effort over the life of a software development project.
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Putnam's software equation is the dynamic multivariable model described in Pressman. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: ____ is not related to Black-box Testing.
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Condition testing exercises the logical conditions in the code – a white-box technique. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The ____ is conducted at the developer's site by a representative group of end users.
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Alpha tests happen at the developer's site; beta tests at the users' sites. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: ____ combines procedures and tools to manage different versions of configuration objects that are created during the software process.
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Pressman's definition of version control. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is true in the context of sparse array?

options.A: The matrices having regular non-zero elements are called unstructured non-zero region matrices.
options.B: Addition of two sparse matrices is possible even if the order of the two matrices are unequal.
options.C: Diagonal matrix and tridiagonal matrix are examples of structured non-zero region matrices.
options.D: Non-zero entries that can occur only on the diagonal or on elements immediately above or below the diagonal is called triangular matrix.

questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Diagonal and tridiagonal matrices have a fixed pattern of non-zero positions; option 4 describes a tridiagonal matrix, and matrices of unequal order cannot be added. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The maximum number of nodes of binary tree at level "i" is ____.
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Each level can have twice as many nodes as the one above: 2^i with the root at level 0 (2^(i−1) if the root is level 1). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which one of the following is false in the context of Divide and Conquer method?

options.D: Subproblems are independent of each other

questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Divide and conquer splits the problem top-down; bottom-up table filling is typical of dynamic programming. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which one of the following technique is not used by the Lower Bound theory for calculating lower bound?
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Horowitz–Sahni: comparison trees, oracles and adversary arguments, and state-space methods; empirical timing does not prove bounds. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is false?

options.A: NP problems are subset of P problems
options.B: NP problems are non-deterministic in nature
options.C: Solution to P class problem is easy to find
options.D: Solutions to NP problems can be verified in polynomial time

questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: P ⊆ NP; whether NP ⊆ P is the open P vs NP question. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: In ____ every even integer greater than 2 can be expressed as the sum of 2 primes.
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Goldbach's conjecture; Lemoine's is about odd numbers as p + 2q. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Determine the correct statements from the following:
I. An approximation algorithm guarantees to run in polynomial time.
II. An approximation algorithm does not guarantee the most effective solution.
III. An approximation algorithm provides solution in exponential time.

options.A: I and II are incorrect; III is correct
options.B: I is correct; II and III are incorrect
options.C: I is incorrect; II and III are correct
options.D: I and II are correct; III is incorrect

questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Approximation algorithms run in polynomial time and give near-optimal, not necessarily optimal, solutions. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: In the vertex cover problem, the optimization problem is to find the vertex cover with ____ and the approximation problem is to find the vertex cover with ____.
questions.subject: Q26–50
questions.explanation: Optimisation seeks the minimum (fewest) cover; an approximation settles for a small (few) one within a guaranteed factor. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: A DPDA is a PDA in which:

options.A: No state has two outgoing transitions
options.B: More than one state can have two or more outgoing transitions
options.C: At least one state has more than one transition
options.D: No state has two incoming transitions

questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: Intended meaning: in a DPDA no configuration has a choice of move – no state has two applicable outgoing transitions for the same input and stack symbol. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The state of a Turing machine when the given input x is not defined on the current state and current input symbol is:
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: If δ is undefined for the current state and symbol, the TM halts. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Consider the Lists A and B of three strings on {0, 1}. If:
X: List A = 1, 10111, 10; List B = 111, 10, 0 and
Y: List A = 10, 011, 101; List B = 101, 11, 011
then which of the following is true?

options.A: Only PCP in X has solution
options.B: Only PCP in Y has solution
options.C: PCP in both X and Y has solution
options.D: PCP neither in X nor in Y has solution

questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: X: indices 2, 1, 1, 3 give 10111·1·1·10 = 101111110 = 10·111·111·0. Y can only start with pair 1 and then B always stays one symbol ahead – no solution (Hopcroft–Ullman). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which of the following derivations is used by top-down parser?
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: Top-down parsers build a leftmost derivation; bottom-up (LR) parsers build a rightmost derivation in reverse. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Choose the correct statement suiting syntax directed definitions from the following:

options.A: Syntax directed definitions + Semantic rules = CFG
options.B: Syntax directed definitions + CFG = Semantic rules
options.C: CFG + Semantic rules = Syntax directed definitions
options.D: CFG + flow graph = syntax directed definitions

questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: An SDD is a context-free grammar together with attributes and semantic rules. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The idea of cache memory is based on the
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: Caches exploit temporal and spatial locality of reference. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which of the following helps Assembler to deal with branching code?
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: The first pass builds the symbol table, so forward branch targets are known in the second pass. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which of the following optimization technique reduces the multiple jumps?
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: Peephole optimisation includes flow-of-control optimisation such as replacing jumps to jumps. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Consider a CSMA/CD network that transmits data at the rate of 100 Mbps (10⁸ bits per second) over 1 km cable without repeaters. Let the minimum frame size required for this network be 1250 bytes. Compute the signal speed of the cable, in terms of km/sec.
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: Frame = 10,000 bits → transmission time 10⁻⁴ s = 2 × propagation time, so propagation = 5 × 10⁻⁵ s for 1 km → 20,000 km/s. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: In Ethernet that uses Manchester encoding, the bit rate is
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: Manchester needs two signal elements per bit, so the baud rate is twice the bit rate. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which layer of OSI reference model is responsible for decomposition of messages and generation of sequence numbers, in order to ensure correct re-composition, from end-to-end of a network?
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: The transport layer segments messages and numbers the segments for end-to-end reassembly. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The divisor in a cyclic code is called
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: The divisor in CRC is the generator polynomial. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: In computer networks, the transmission media are generally categorized as:
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: Guided (cables) and unguided (wireless) media. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The port number of POP is:
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: POP3 uses TCP port 110 (995 over TLS). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: A piece of icon or image on a webpage, associated with another webpage is called
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: Any text or image that links to another resource is a hyperlink. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The acronym DVMRP stands for:
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: DVMRP is a multicast routing protocol based on distance-vector routing. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Artificial Intelligence is a ____ approach which can make decisions based on logical reasoning and problem solving strategies.
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: Russell & Norvig: AI as building rational agents that act to achieve the best expected outcome. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Identify the atomic proposition in the following statements:
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: A proposition is a declarative sentence that is true or false; commands, exclamations and open statements with variables are not. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: ____ search is performed by exploring all nodes at a given depth before proceeding to the next level.
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: Breadth-first search expands level by level. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which type of knowledge representation does not exhibit any learning capabilities?
questions.subject: Q51–75
questions.explanation: This is the answer in KEA's revised key. (Official answer: KEA revised key, 28 Mar 2024.)

questions.question: What is the role of pragmatics in Natural Language Processing?

options.B: To find contextual meaning and implied communication
options.C: To identify syntax errors in the text
options.D: To find morphological analysis of words

questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Pragmatics interprets meaning in context (intent, implicature). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which algorithm considers all moves from current state and selects the best move as the next state?
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Steepest-ascent hill climbing examines all neighbours and moves to the best one; simple hill climbing takes the first better one. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Backpropagation Neural Network is a technique used for:

options.A: Transmission of error back through the network to adjust the inputs
options.B: Updating weights based on error propagation
options.C: Updating the number of hidden layers

questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Backpropagation propagates the error gradient backwards to update the weights (not the inputs). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which of the following introduces non-linearity into neural network?
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: ReLU is the standard non-linear activation used in trainable networks; convolution and identity are linear, and the step function has no useful gradient. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The most appropriate logical expression for the sentence "You cannot use the waterslide if you are under 48 inches in height unless you are older than 14 years old" is (q: you can use the waterslide, r: you are under 48 inches, s: you are older than 14):
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Rosen's example: if under 48 inches and not older than 14, then you cannot ride: (r ∧ ¬s) → ¬q. (The letters are Rosen's; the paper uses them without defining them.) (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Find out which rule of inference is used in the argument "The meeting has been rescheduled and the conference room is empty now. Therefore, the meeting has been rescheduled now".
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: From p ∧ q conclude p – simplification. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: A relation R on a set S is called ____ if it is reflexive, antisymmetric and transitive.
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Reflexive + antisymmetric + transitive = partial order; reflexive + symmetric + transitive = equivalence relation. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: R1 lacks (3,1) for (3,4),(4,1); R2 lacks (2,2) for (2,1),(1,2); R3 lacks (4,2) for (4,1),(1,2). R4 (>), R5 (≤) and R6 are transitive. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: In how many ways can 10 examination answer papers be arranged so that the best and worst papers never come together?
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: All arrangements 10! minus those with the two together 2 × 9! = 9!(10 − 2) = 8 × 9!. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: ____ is not necessarily a property of a group.

options.A: Existence of inverse for every element

questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Groups need closure, associativity, identity and inverses; commutativity makes it abelian. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Consider the set S = {1, ω, ω²} where ω and ω² are cube roots of unity. If * denotes the multiplication operation, then the structure of (S, *) forms
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: S is closed under multiplication (ω³ = 1), with identity 1 and inverses ω ↔ ω²; one operation only, so a group (cyclic of order 3). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which of the following Euler circuit is impossible if number of vertices is greater than 2?
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: In a wheel every rim vertex has degree 3 (odd), so no Euler circuit; Cₙ always has one, Kₙ for odd n, Qₙ for even n. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Consider a complete graph G with 5 vertices. The graph G has ____ spanning trees.
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Cayley's formula nⁿ⁻² = 5³ = 125. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The amount of time by which an activity can be delayed without affecting project completion time is:
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Total float is the delay that does not delay the project; free float does not delay the next activity. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Select the equivalent of NOR gate from the following (the paper shows gate symbols):

options.B: AND gate with both inputs inverted
options.C: OR gate with both inputs inverted
options.D: AND gate with both inputs and the output inverted

questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: De Morgan: (A + B)′ = A′·B′, an AND gate with inverted inputs. Option 3 equals NAND and option 4 equals OR. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The register used as a working area in CPU is
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: The accumulator holds operands and intermediate results. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which of the following architecture is used in Modern computers?
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: General-purpose computers follow the stored-program von Neumann model (with Harvard-style split caches internally). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The primary objective of assembly language is:

options.B: To simplify programming by providing high level language constructs.
options.C: To provide a way to interact with hardware at a low level.
options.D: To provide a way to interact with hardware at a high level.

questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Assembly gives symbolic access to machine instructions and registers. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: In Microprogrammed Control, the data register is sometimes called
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Mano: the control data register is sometimes called a pipeline register. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Specify the control word to perform addition between R2 and R3 and the result will be stored in R1.
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Mano's 14-bit control word SELA|SELB|SELD|OPR: R2 = 010, R3 = 011, R1 = 001, ADD = 00010 → 010 011 001 00010. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: In which addressing mode, the effective address is equal to the address part of the instruction?
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: In direct addressing the instruction's address field is the effective address. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: In asynchronous serial data transfer, we use ____ number of flag bits.
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Each character is framed by a start bit and a stop bit. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Hit ratio of cache memory is defined as

options.A: Number of hits divided by total number of hits and misses.
options.B: Number of hits divided by number of misses.
options.C: Number of hits plus misses divided by number of hits.
options.D: Number of misses divided by number of hits.

questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 2, 3, 3 give ab·ba·aa·aa = abbaaaaa on top and abb·aaa·a·a = abbaaaaa below. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Flow of information among the attributes in a parse tree is denoted by
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: A dependency graph shows the order in which attribute instances must be evaluated. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The optional access link in the activation record is used for

options.A: pointing to the activation record of the cache
options.B: referring non-local data held in other activation records

questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: The access (static) link points to the activation record of the enclosing scope, for access to non-local names. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The primary data structure used by an LR parser to keep track of the parsing process is ____
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: An LR parser shifts states and symbols onto a stack and pops them on reductions. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: If a carrier modulated by a digital bit stream has one of the possible phases of 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees, such modulation is called as
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Four phases, each carrying 2 bits, is quadrature phase-shift keying. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Match the following for IPv4 addressing and select the correct key
a) class A
b) class B
c) class C
d) class D
(i) 2 bytes for network portion, 2 bytes for host portion
(ii) multicasting
(iii) 1 byte for network portion, 3 bytes for host portion
(iv) 3 portions for network portion, 1 byte for host portion

options.A: a – iv, b – i, c – iii, d – ii
options.B: a – iii, b – i, c – iv, d – ii
options.C: a – ii, b – iii, c – i, d – iv
options.D: a – iv, b – ii, c – iii, d – i

questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Class A = 8 network bits, class B = 16, class C = 24; class D addresses are for multicast. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: A bridge operates at the data link layer giving it access to the ____ address of all the stations connected to it.
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: A bridge works at layer 2 and filters frames using physical (MAC) addresses. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: For a network with n devices, the number of duplex-mode links required for mesh topology is:
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Every pair needs one duplex link: C(n, 2) = n(n − 1)/2. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The process of dividing an analog signal into a string of discrete outputs, each denoting a constant amplitude is called as
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Quantisation maps sampled amplitudes onto a finite set of levels. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: When data and acknowledgement are sent in a same frame, it is known as
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Piggybacking attaches the acknowledgement to an outgoing data frame. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The role of Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) is to find the

options.C: IP address that corresponds to a MAC address
options.D: MAC address that corresponds to an IP address

questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: ARP maps a known IP address to a MAC address on the local network (RARP does the reverse). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Which of these are TRUE for public-private key encryption algorithm?
(i) Private key of the receiver is used by the sender to encrypt the message
(ii) Public key is used by the receiver to decrypt the message
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: The sender encrypts with the receiver's public key and the receiver decrypts with its own private key. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Which of these statements are CORRECT?
(i) When a router receives the packet, TTL is reduced by one
(ii) When a router receives the packet, TTL is increased by one
(iii) If the TTL count is zero and the packet has not reached the destination, the packet is discarded
(iv) If the TTL count is 255 and the packet has not reached the destination, the packet is discarded
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Each router decrements TTL and discards the packet when TTL reaches zero. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The Mobile Application Part (MAP) is a/an ____ protocol that provides an application layer for the various nodes in GSM and UMTS mobile core networks and GPRS core networks.
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: MAP is an application-layer protocol of the SS7 (Signalling System No. 7) stack. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: What is the Turing Test designed to assess?
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Turing's imitation game tests whether a machine's conversational behaviour is indistinguishable from a human's. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Suppose you are constructing AI for an intergalactic travel planner. What representation handles multiple planets?

options.A: Stacking planets in a priority queue based on their beauty
options.B: A graph connecting planets with worm hole edges for quick travel
options.C: A hash table mapping planets to their languages
options.D: An array of codes to encode planet coordinates

questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Route planning needs locations as vertices and connections as edges – a graph. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which one of the following is used to query RDF in semantic web?
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: SPARQL is the W3C query language for RDF data. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which technique considers the problem of extracting a reward function from observed optimal behaviour of an expert acting in an environment?
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Inverse RL infers the reward from demonstrations; ordinary RL learns behaviour from a given reward. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Fuzzy equivalence relation is a type of fuzzy relation that satisfies
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Like a crisp equivalence relation, a fuzzy equivalence (similarity) relation is reflexive, symmetric and (max–min) transitive. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: In a multilayer perceptron, the back propagation algorithm is used

options.A: As it initializes the weights of networks
options.D: To propagate errors back through network to update the weights

questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Backpropagation computes error gradients layer by layer, backwards, for weight updates. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which one of the following is not a specified method that is used for the selection of parents?
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Elitism copies the best individuals unchanged into the next generation; it is not a parent-selection scheme. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which one of the following algorithm is commonly used for classification tasks in AI?
questions.subject: Q76–100
questions.explanation: Decision trees are supervised classifiers; K-means is unsupervised clustering. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)
